newsitem.title: UK: Clyde sees 9 pct production rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Clyde sees 9 pct production rise in 1997.

text.p: Bid target Clyde Petroleum Plc said it expected production to rise by nine percent to an average 44,900 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd).
The group, which faces a 432 million stg bid from Gulf Canada Resources, believes production will increase to an average 55,200 boepd in 1998 and 60,200 in 1999.
Clyde earlier reported a 21.7 percent rise in 1996 earnings to 32 million stg thanks to increased production and higher oil and gas prices.
Clyde, which again advised shareholders to reject Gulf Canada's offer, said it was looking for new venture opportunities in Australia after acquiring Crusader Ltd last year.

"Clyde's strategy is to increase production and reserves in order to sustain earnings and cash flow growth, through a balanced programme of acquisition, development and exploration," Clyde said in a statement accompanying its 1996 results.
